description: Author-curated knowledge base used to constrain LLM guidance generation (manuscript Supplementary Table S3). Each entry is paraphrased from the cited source; citations were compiled by the authors.

urgency_levels.1: Primary care or optometry within 1 week

entries.name: Normal Eye
entries.condition_summary: Normal external ocular appearance without significant conjunctival injection, hemorrhage, eyelid pathology, or obvious inflammatory findings.
entries.initial_management: Reassurance if asymptomatic. Continue evaluation if symptoms are disproportionate to examination findings.
entries.consultation_urgency: Self-care / observation unless concerning symptoms are present.

entries.name: Viral Conjunctivitis
entries.condition_summary: Common self-limited conjunctival inflammation, most often caused by adenovirus. Highly contagious but generally not sight-threatening.
typical_clinical_features: Often starts unilateral then becomes bilateral
red_flags: Contact lens wearer with worsening symptoms
entries.initial_management: Artificial tears, cool compresses, hand hygiene, avoidance of contact lenses, and supportive care.
entries.consultation_urgency: Routine unless red flags are present.

entries.name: Bacterial Conjunctivitis
entries.condition_summary: Acute conjunctival infection characterized by mucopurulent discharge and conjunctival redness.
entries.initial_management: Topical antibiotic therapy may be considered depending on severity and patient factors; maintain hygiene and avoid contact lenses.
entries.consultation_urgency: Routine unless corneal involvement or red flags are present.

entries.name: Allergic Conjunctivitis
entries.condition_summary: IgE-mediated conjunctival inflammation associated with environmental allergens.
entries.initial_management: Allergen avoidance, lubricating drops, antihistamine drops, and cool compresses.

entries.name: Episcleritis
entries.condition_summary: Benign inflammation of the episcleral tissue that is typically self-limited and non-sight-threatening.
entries.initial_management: Artificial tears and supportive care; evaluate for underlying systemic disease if recurrent.
entries.consultation_urgency: Ophthalmology within 24–48 hours if diagnosis is uncertain.

citations.source: AAO Basic and Clinical Science Course

entries.name: Scleritis
entries.condition_summary: Deep scleral inflammation frequently associated with autoimmune disease and potentially vision-threatening.
typical_clinical_features: Pain radiating to face or jaw
entries.initial_management: Urgent ophthalmology evaluation and systemic workup.

citations.source: AAO Basic and Clinical Science Course

entries.name: Anterior Uveitis
entries.condition_summary: Inflammation of the iris and ciliary body that may be associated with autoimmune disease and can threaten vision if untreated.
entries.initial_management: Urgent ophthalmology assessment. Avoid empiric corticosteroids unless directed by ophthalmology.

entries.name: Subconjunctival Hemorrhage
entries.condition_summary: Bleeding beneath the bulbar conjunctiva producing a sharply demarcated red patch. Usually benign and self-resolving.
entries.initial_management: Observation and reassurance. Artificial tears if irritation is present.
entries.consultation_urgency: Routine unless red flags are present.

entries.name: Hordeolum (Stye)
entries.condition_summary: Acute bacterial infection of an eyelid gland resulting in a localized tender eyelid nodule.
entries.initial_management: Warm compresses several times daily and eyelid hygiene.

entries.name: Chalazion
entries.condition_summary: Chronic granulomatous inflammation of a meibomian gland causing a painless eyelid lump.

entries.name: Blepharitis
entries.condition_summary: Chronic inflammation of the eyelid margins commonly associated with meibomian gland dysfunction.
entries.initial_management: Lid hygiene, warm compresses, and artificial tears.

entries.name: Preseptal Cellulitis
entries.condition_summary: Infection of tissues anterior to the orbital septum causing eyelid erythema and swelling without orbital involvement.

entries.name: Orbital Cellulitis
entries.condition_summary: Infection involving tissues posterior to the orbital septum. Vision- and life-threatening emergency.
entries.initial_management: Emergency referral for imaging, intravenous antibiotics, and ophthalmology consultation.

entries.name: Infectious Keratitis / Corneal Ulcer
entries.condition_summary: Corneal infection that can rapidly threaten vision and requires urgent ophthalmologic evaluation.
entries.initial_management: Immediate ophthalmology referral and discontinuation of contact lens use.

citations.source: AAO Preferred Practice Pattern: Bacterial Keratitis

entries.name: Acute Angle-Closure Glaucoma
entries.condition_summary: Acute obstruction of aqueous outflow causing rapid elevation of intraocular pressure and vision-threatening injury.
entries.initial_management: Immediate emergency ophthalmology assessment and intraocular pressure reduction.

citations.source: AAO Preferred Practice Pattern: Primary Angle Closure Disease
